name: nub
description: TypeScript-first developer supertool — a Rust CLI that augments your Node.js
comment: @oxc-project/runtime is pinned to an EXACT version (no caret) and MUST match the oxc version compiled into nub's native addon (crates/nub-native, see OXC_VERSION in Cargo.toml) — it supplies the transpile emit's runtime helpers (e.g. usingCtx for `using` down-leveling), so it is one half of an oxc release whose other half (the transformer + parser) is now native, not an npm package. The transpiler and TS/JSX detection moved in-process to nub-native, so oxc-transform and oxc-parser are no longer dependencies; only the helper-runtime package remains, imported by transpiled user code via VENDORED_PACKAGES. NUB_VERSION is the sole transpile-cache-busting key (runtime/preload.mjs); `make version` bumps it and rebuilds the addon, keeping the cache invariant 'the transpiler version is a pure function of the nub version'. Bump @oxc-project/runtime in lockstep with the addon's oxc pin. See wiki/runtime/transpile-cache.md. SEPARATELY, on adding any root dependency: every ci.yml test leg runs this file's `npm ci` through the Socket Firewall shim, and an sfw crash that exits 0 leaves a half-built tree behind a GREEN install step — the following 'assert root deps actually installed' step is what catches it. A large addition (~185 packages, measured) trips that guard across the whole matrix, and the symptom looks like unrelated import failures. Prefer `npx` at a pinned version for tooling that is not imported by the runtime; lat.md's checker is wired that way in the `lat:check` script. SEPARATELY, on "devEngines": the root deps are npm-managed (every CI leg runs `npm ci`), but the root also carries a bun.lock for cross-PM dogfooding — see the two-lockfile check in scripts/check-oxc-lockstep.mjs. Two candidate lockfiles and no declaration make this an ambiguous project, which `nub install` refuses with ERR_NUB_LOCKFILE_AMBIGUOUS — nub could not install its own repo. `devEngines.packageManager` is the tie-break, and it is the version-free declaration on purpose: `packageManager` pins an exact npm, and the yarn-pnp CI job runs `corepack enable`, which would then try to fetch that pin. Keep the field free of extra keys — npm validates devEngines strictly and dies on an unknown one (Invalid property devEngines.comment), which is why this note lives here instead.
